pairs: Viro qui corripientem dura cervice contemnit, repentinus ei superveniet interitus, et eum sanitas non sequetur.
The man who, with a stiff neck, treats the one who corrects him with contempt will be suddenly overwhelmed to his own destruction, and reason shall not follow him.
In multiplicatione justorum lætabitur vulgus;
When just men are multiplied, the common people shall rejoice.
cum impii sumpserint principatum,
When the impious take up the leadership,
gemet populus.
the people shall mourn.
Vir qui amat sapientiam lætificat patrem suum;
The man who loves wisdom rejoices his father.
qui autem nutrit scorta perdet substantiam.
But whoever nurtures promiscuous women will lose his substance.
Rex justus erigit terram;
A just king guides the land.
vir avarus destruet eam.
A man of avarice will destroy it.
Homo qui blandis fictisque sermonibus loquitur amico suo rete expandit gressibus ejus.
A man who speaks to his friend with flattering and feigned words spreads a net for his own feet.
Peccantem virum iniquum involvet laqueus,
A snare will entangle the iniquitous when he sins.
et justus laudabit atque gaudebit.
And the just shall praise and be glad.
Novit justus causam pauperum;
The just knows the case of the poor.
impius ignorat scientiam.
The impious is ignorant of knowledge.
Homines pestilentes dissipant civitatem;
Pestilent men squander a city.
sapientes vero avertunt furorem.
Yet truly, the wise avert fury.
Vir sapiens si cum stulto contenderit,
A wise man,
sive irascatur,
if he were to contend with the foolish,
sive rideat,
whether in anger or in laughter,
non inveniet requiem.
would find no rest.
Viri sanguinum oderunt simplicem;
Bloodthirsty men hate the simple one;
justi autem quærunt animam ejus.
but the just seek out his soul.
Totum spiritum suum profert stultus;
A foolish one offers everything on his mind.
sapiens differt,
A wise one reserves
et reservat in posterum.
and defers until later.
Princeps qui libenter audit verba mendacii, omnes ministros habet impios.
A leader who freely listens to lying words has only impious servants.
Pauper et creditor obviaverunt sibi:
The pauper and the creditor have met one another.
utriusque illuminator est Dominus.
The Lord is the illuminator of them both.
Rex qui judicat in veritate pauperes,
The king who judges the poor in truth,
thronus ejus in æternum firmabitur.
his throne shall be secured in eternity.
Virga
The rod and its correction distribute wisdom.
atque correptio tribuit sapientiam;
But the child who is left to his own will,
puer autem qui dimittitur voluntati suæ confundit matrem suam.
brings shame to his mother.
In multiplicatione impiorum multiplicabuntur scelera,
When the impious are multiplied, crimes will be multiplied.
et justi ruinas eorum videbunt.
But the just shall see their ruin.
Erudi filium tuum,
Teach your son,
et refrigerabit te,
and he will refresh you,
et dabit delicias animæ tuæ.
and he will give delight to your soul.
Cum prophetia defecerit, dissipabitur populus;
When prophecy fails, the people will be scattered.
qui vero custodit legem beatus est.
Yet truly, whoever guards the law is blessed.
Servus verbis non potest erudiri,
A servant cannot be taught by words,
quia quod dicis intelligit,
because he understands what you say,
et respondere contemnit.
but he disdains to respond.
Vidisti hominem velocem ad loquendum?
Have you seen a man rushing to speak?
stultitia magis speranda est quam illius correptio.
Foolishness has more hope than his correction.
Qui delicate a pueritia nutrit servum suum postea sentiet eum contumacem.
Whoever nurtures his servant delicately from childhood, afterwards will find him defiant.
Vir iracundus provocat rixas,
A short-tempered man provokes quarrels.
et qui ad indignandum facilis est erit ad peccandum proclivior.
And whoever is easily angered is more likely to sin.
Superbum sequitur humilitas,
Humiliation follows the arrogant.
et humilem spiritu suscipiet gloria.
And glory shall uphold the humble in spirit.
Qui cum fure participat odit animam suam;
Whoever participates with a thief hates his own soul;
adjurantem audit,
for he listens to his oath
et non indicat.
and does not denounce him.
Qui timet hominem cito corruet;
Whoever fears man will quickly fall.
qui sperat in Domino sublevabitur.
Whoever hopes in the Lord shall be lifted up.
Multi requirunt faciem principis,
Many demand the face of the leader.
et judicium a Domino egreditur singulorum.
But the judgment of each one proceeds from the Lord.
Abominantur justi virum impium,
The just abhor an impious man.
et abominantur impii eos qui in recta sunt via.
And the impious abhor those who are on the right way.
Verbum custodiens filius extra perditionem erit.
By keeping the word, the son shall be free from perdition.
